subject: Re: Dedicated Onboarding Rebate & Throughput Smoothing
messages:
From: Diego Ruiz <diego.ruiz@helios.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@helios.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring Dedicated migration economics and short-term smoothing

Tessa —

Thanks for the product overview last week. We liked the Dedicated model but need clarity on economics for a hosted->dedicated migration. Two quick asks from our side: 1) what conversion credit you can apply to our billed Hosted spend to offset the first 3 months of Dedicated commit; 2) a short-term bridge that smooths throughput mismatches while our GPU pool is ramping (we expect bursty batches during launch).

High level: Helios expects to commit to a 12-month reserved pool (NVIDIA A100-equivalent) targeting sustained 1200 tokens/sec for our inference workload with P95 latency <120ms. We want to understand: how many GPUs you recommend, what SLAs you can guarantee for 95th percentile, and whether you can offer a temporary rebate or credit to cover the two-month run rate delta.

Procurement is copied for timing/PO questions. Happy to share a simple token/profile dump if that helps sizing.

—Diego
Head of Product, Helios Robotics
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Diego Ruiz <diego.ruiz@helios.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-23T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring Dedicated migration economics and short-term smoothing

Diego —

Appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers up front and then a proposed next step:

- Conversion credit: we typically offer a hosted-spend conversion credit applied pro rata to the first 2 months of Dedicated billing; for a 12-month commit we can extend to 3 months for a modest additional discount (details below).
- Bridge smoothing: we can provide 2 bridge months of reduced committed billing (50% billed) while you ramp, plus auto-burst into shared capacity for spikes.
- Sizing: based on your target 1200 tokens/sec and P95 <120ms, preliminary estimate is a pool of 4 x L40-like GPUs with continuous batching + KV cache; final number depends on sequence length distribution and mix of prompt vs. streaming inference.
- SLA: we can commit to 99.9% availability for the Dedicated pool and a throughput warranty for reserved capacity; we will document P95 latency targets in an SLA exhibit (attached).

I've attached a proposed commit schedule and our SLA exhibit. Aditya — can you pull hosted spend numbers and draft a conversion-credit amount we can offer (we should consider Helios' ARR and expected ramp). Karthik — please flag anything from procurement/contract shape perspective.

If Helios can share a token profile, we'll do a short sizing run and firm up the GPU count and commit needed. Can we schedule a 30-min call this week?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Diego Ruiz <diego.ruiz@helios.ai>, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-24T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring Dedicated migration economics and short-term smoothing

Diego —

Thanks — I pulled Helios' last 6 months of hosted billings (summary attached) and ran a quick conversion propose:

- Baseline: for a 12-month commit at 4 GPUs (L40 equiv), list price $X/month.
- Conversion credit offer: credit equal to 60% of your average hosted spend for the two months prior to sign, applied as a dollar credit across the first 3 invoices (de-rates over 3 months: 40% / 35% / 25%).
- Optional: extend the credit to cover 3 full months if Helios accepts a 12% uplift on the commit (adds predictability on our side).
- Bridge months: first 2 months billed at 50% of committed monthly fee; burst into hosted pool for excess at hosted rates.
- True-up: quarter cadence true-up based on realized throughput; shortfall protection available with a cap (we'd discuss the cap based on final sizing).

Open items we need from Helios to finalize: sequence length histogram, typical batch sizes, and target concurrency. I linked a short sizing template in the drive folder.

Attachments: proposed-commit-schedule.xlsx, helios_mop_v1.pdf

—Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Diego Ruiz <diego.ruiz@helios.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@helios.ai, sales@cloudreseller.com
Date: 2026-08-28T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring Dedicated migration economics and short-term smoothing

Aditya/Tessa —

Thanks for the draft, it helps. A few procurement points from our side:

1) We need a clearer breakdown showing net effective price over the first 6 months (hosted baseline vs. dedicated with credits + bridge). Can you provide a 6-month cashflow view?
2) Regarding the credit schedule: Helios prefers a heavier upfront conversion (front-load) rather than a long tail. Would Redwood consider a 70%/20%/10% split across the first three invoices?
3) True-up cadence: quarterly is ok but procurement requests a 30-day visibility window for any true-up bill so we can plan budgets; can that be accommodated?
4) Contract clause: we need a ramp-exit clause if production performance (P95) is not met after the first 60 days post-cutover.

We can share the token/sample profile by EOD tomorrow. Also copying our channel partner (CloudReseller) to confirm discount stacking and marketplace terms.

—Diego
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Diego Ruiz <diego.ruiz@helios.ai>, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-01T14:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring Dedicated migration economics and short-term smoothing

Diego / team —

Appreciate the constructive asks. I reviewed the deal and can approve a one-time exception to better align the credit profile with Helios' request. Final summary of what Redwood can commit:

- Conversion credit: 70% / 20% / 10% applied to the first three dedicated invoices (as requested). Total credit capped at the historical hosted spend for the prior 60 days.
- Bridge months: first 2 months billed at 50% of committed fee; during these months, Helios will be permitted to burst into hosted capacity subject to hosted-rate overage fees.
- True-up: quarterly true-up retained, plus a 30-day heads-up window for anticipated shortfalls (we will implement automated usage forecasts to notify you).
- SLA / ramp-exit: Redwood will include an SLA exhibit with a 60-day performance review. If P95 latency target is missed for two consecutive weekly samples after cutover and remediation fails, Helios may invoke a ramp-exit option (detailed in DocuSign exhibit).
- Discount/partner stacking: we'll honor marketplace/partner discounts validated by CloudReseller; channel credits will be considered additive to the conversion credit but net capped so total effective discount does not exceed 40% of list for the first 3 months.

Next steps: Tessa/Aditya will update the commit schedule spreadsheet with the 70/20/10 credit profile and a 6-month cashflow column and share a DocuSign pull for the SLA exhibit. Please confirm receipt and availability for a Tuesday sign-off call.

—Lauren Bishop
VP, Commercial Sales, Redwood Inference
